- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or 10% below true peak.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates 30d horizon; apply 3–5% downward adjustment for bullish sentiment.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often underestimates mean reversion; add 2–5% to forecast to account for lagged correction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion within 7–14 days, model tends to overpredict continuation; adjust forecast downward by 3–8% for 10–14 day horizon.
- For sentiment history with repeated negative spikes, model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 30d horizon.
